add.issue.name: Fix: autosync clobbers time-travel checkout via a TOCTOU race (getGuiState() re-check after async sync)

edit.description.md:
Requirement (user, verbatim intent): "when I check out old state I keep geting sent back to live state. I think this is because there is some sync happening even if I am in detached 'read only state'... can you investigate..."

Root cause confirmed: `source/gui/api/lib/api-autosync.ts`'s `runSync()` checks `getTimeTravelStatus().mode !== 'live'` only ONCE, before `await sync({repoRoot})` — a real network git pull/push that can take anywhere from tens of ms to seconds. `sync()` itself doesn't touch the state singleton (confirmed by reading `mcp/epiq-api.ts`'s `sync` export — it's pure git pull/push + sync-status bookkeeping). But immediately after it resolves, `runSync` unconditionally calls `getGuiState()` (which `boot()`s — unconditionally re-materializes live state from the event log) and broadcasts the result to every client, with no re-check. If a `time-travel:scrub` websocket message is processed during that async gap (fully plausible — the 15s interval fires regardless of user activity), the historical checkout gets silently overwritten and broadcast back to live the moment the in-flight sync finishes. This also likely explains the "stale/wrong state on first load" flakiness observed repeatedly during earlier manual browser testing this session, previously (incorrectly) written off as a browser-automation timing artifact.

Fix: a proper async mutex shared between checkoutStateAt/returnToLive (epiq-time-travel.ts) and runSync (api-autosync.ts) so the two operations can never interleave — whichever starts first runs to completion (including its broadcast) before the other begins, and each re-reads the live/scrub mode fresh at the moment it actually acquires the lock rather than trusting a stale pre-await check.

add.issue.comment.md:
Found a broader instance of the same bug while verifying the autosync fix: `getGuiState()` (mcp/epiq-api.ts) unconditionally calls `boot()` — re-materializing live state — on every call, and it's called from more than just autosync: `websocket.ts`'s `state:get` handler (fires on every client connect/reconnect, and via the client's `requestState()` retry path), plus several api-server.ts HTTP endpoints including the plain GET `/api/state`. Any of these firing while scrubbing would silently clobber the checkout the same way autosync did — a client reconnect alone (e.g. a network blip) would be enough, no sync required.

Fixing at the source: make `getGuiState()` itself skip `boot()` and fall back to `deriveGuiState()` when time-travel mode isn't live, so every call site is safe automatically instead of relying on each caller to remember to guard.

add.issue.name: MCP read calls can hang the server via implicit git pull SSH auth (GH #80)
Document/fix registry-independent MCP launcher for restricted envs (GH #79)

edit.description.md:
On Linux, `epiq_board_list` (and other read-only MCP calls) run `git pull --ff-only` implicitly. If the MCP host doesn't pass `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` through, SSH opens `/dev/tty` to prompt for auth, which triggers SIGTTIN and stops the whole Epiq MCP server process group. The server stays hung until the client's tool timeout or a manual kill, and it looks persistent across sessions since a new conversation can reuse the stopped process.

Reported by a user on epiq 1.3.3 / MCP server 0.2.30, Codex MCP client, SSH remote repo.

Suggested fixes from the reporter:
- Avoid remote git sync on every read-only call, or make it explicit/configurable
- Ensure git auth failures return a bounded tool error instead of letting job control stop the server
- Consider `GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o BatchMode=yes"` for non-interactive git ops
- Document that MCP hosts may need `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` passed explicitly

Source: https://github.com/ljtn/epiq/issues/80

The documented launcher `npx -y -p epiq epiq-mcp` always attempts npm registry resolution at startup, even if the package is already cached locally. In network-restricted agent sandboxes this causes DNS retries (EAI_AGAIN) that delay MCP init with no useful MCP-level error, making the server look hung.

Reported by a user on epiq 1.3.3, Linux, restricted-network MCP host. `npx --offline` didn't help. Workaround: install `epiq@1.3.3` globally and point the MCP config directly at the resolved executable — initializes immediately.

Suggested fixes from the reporter:
- Document a pinned direct-executable install as the recommended option for sandboxed/offline environments
- Keep `npx` for convenient online setup, but note it may hit the npm registry on every process start
- If feasible, provide a launcher that fails fast with a clear registry-resolution error instead of hanging

Source: https://github.com/ljtn/epiq/issues/79

add.issue.comment.md:
Worked this on branch `fix/79-mcp-registry-independent-launcher`. Scope: documentation only — added a "Sandboxed or network-restricted environments" subsection to the MCP & Agent Compatibility section of `readme.md`, recommending `npm install --global epiq` + pointing the MCP config at the resolved `epiq-mcp` binary path directly, as an alternative to `npx -y -p epiq epiq-mcp`.

**Testing / findings:**

1. **Direct binary has zero network dependency.** Built `dist/mcp.js` via `npm run build:npm` and ran it directly (`node dist/mcp.js --help`) — consistently starts in ~0.2-0.3s regardless of network/registry state. Confirmed with `npm link` producing a real `epiq-mcp` binary symlink (`~/.npm-global/bin/epiq-mcp`) that also starts instantly under an unreachable-registry config.

2. **`npx --offline` fails outright on a cold cache**, matching the reporter's experience. Using an isolated `$HOME`/npm cache (no prior epiq metadata), `npx --offline -y -p epiq epiq-mcp --help` fails immediately with `command not found` (exit 127) — there's no local metadata to resolve from, so `--offline` isn't a usable escape hatch once the cache is empty. This confirms the reporter's note that `--offline` "didn't help because npm lacked the registry metadata needed to resolve the package."

3. **`npm link` / global install needs no registry access at all** — it's a local filesystem operation. Ran `npm link` against a deliberately unreachable registry URL and it still succeeded, producing a working `epiq-mcp` binary. This is why the documented workaround (global install once, then point the MCP config at the resolved path) sidesteps the problem entirely: registry access is only needed at install time (and can happen from a network-connected machine, then be reused/copied), never at MCP server startup.

4. **Could not fully reproduce the exact hang mechanics** (`EAI_AGAIN` / multi-second DNS retries) described in the report. On macOS, unreachable/invalid registry hosts (including RFC 2606 `.invalid` TLDs and unreachable local ports) fail fast rather than retrying — `EAI_AGAIN` specifically implies a *transient* DNS failure (e.g. UDP:53 packets silently dropped by a sandbox firewall), which requires an environment where DNS queries time out rather than get an immediate NXDOMAIN/refused response. I didn't attempt to reproduce that at the OS/firewall level since it would require modifying system DNS/firewall behavior on this machine. The *effect* (npx blocking on registry resolution when only `npx`/cache-based resolution is used) is real and independent of the exact retry mechanism, so the documented fix (avoid npx's registry dependency altogether via a direct executable) addresses the root cause either way.

**Suggested follow-up (not done here, out of scope for a docs fix):** the reporter's other two suggestions — (a) a launcher that fails fast with a clear registry-resolution error instead of hanging, and (b) potentially bundling/publishing a non-npx quickstart script — would need actual code changes to `install.sh` or a new bin wrapper. Leaving this ticket's code scope to docs for now; happy to split those into a follow-up if wanted.

add.issue.comment.md:
Worked this on branch `fix/80-mcp-ssh-auth-hang` (from `main`). Two changes, both addressing the reporter's suggested fixes directly.

**Root cause confirmed:** every MCP tool call (read or write) goes through a shared `boot()` in `source/mcp/epiq-api.ts` that unconditionally runs `git pull --ff-only` via `execGit` (`source/git/git-utils.ts`). `execGit`'s spawn env sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_ASKPASS=echo`, but those only silence *git's* own prompts — they don't touch `ssh`, which still opens `/dev/tty` when no agent/key is usable. In a backgrounded process group (the MCP server), that tty-open triggers `SIGTTIN` and stops the whole process, exactly as reported — the existing 10s timeout+`SIGTERM` never gets a chance to run because a *stopped* process doesn't process signals or timers.

**Fix 1 — harden the SSH invocation itself** (`source/git/git-utils.ts`): added `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10` to the shared git spawn env (respects a caller-provided `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` if already set). `BatchMode=yes` disables all interactive password/passphrase querying at the ssh level — the reporter's suggested fix #3 — so ssh fails fast instead of opening `/dev/tty`. `ConnectTimeout=10` additionally bounds a related but separate hang mode: a network-level black hole (packets silently dropped) rather than a prompt. Verified directly: without these options, `ssh` to a black-holed IP was still hanging past 15s; with them, it fails in exactly 10.0s (`ssh: connect ... Operation timed out`).

**Fix 2 — stop syncing on reads at all** (`source/mcp/epiq-api.ts`): per the reporter's suggested fix #1 (and raised independently during review), `boot()` now takes an optional `{pull: boolean}` (default `true` for compatibility). The read-only MCP tools — `listBoards`, `listSwimlanes`, `listIssues`, `getEpiqState`, `getAttachmentBlob` — now pass `{pull: false}`, so they never touch the network at all; they just read whatever's already local. Fetching remote changes stays available on-demand via the existing `epiq_sync` tool (`sync()` already does its own explicit `syncEpiqWithRemote`, independent of `boot()`). Write tools (`createIssue`, `closeIssue`, etc.) keep pulling before applying an event, unchanged.

One read-ish call, `getGuiState`, was deliberately **left pulling** — it's what the GUI's ~15s autosync loop (`source/gui/api/lib/api-autosync.ts`) calls to keep multi-user browser state fresh in near-real-time, so disabling that would regress real-time collaboration. Left a comment in the code explaining why it's the odd one out.

- New regression test in `source/test/git-utils.test.ts`: asserts `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` defaults to `BatchMode=yes`.
- New regression tests in `source/mcp/test/epiq-api.test.ts`: asserts `execGit` is never called with `pull` args for `listBoards`/`listSwimlanes`/`listIssues`/`getEpiqState`, and still is for `createIssue`.

add.issue.name: Event userIds are lowercased by the log filename round-trip

edit.description.md:
Root cause of the contributor case variance. Not historical drift — it happens on every event written today.

The event log file is named `${sanitizeFilePart(userId)}.${sanitizeFilePart(userName)}.jsonl`, and `sanitizeFilePart` (event-persist.ts:70) lowercases — correct for a filename, since filesystems vary in case sensitivity. But on load, `event-load.ts:28` reconstructs the actor by parsing that filename:

    const [userId, userName] = path.basename(filePath, '.jsonl').split('.');

So the lowercased filename becomes the authoritative userId for every event, discarding the real casing. Measured on this repo: all 765 events carry lowercase userIds, the most recent from today. The uppercase ids that appear alongside them come from contributor registry nodes, which are created with `ulid()` directly and never make that round-trip — which is exactly why one person renders twice.

Corroborating: `isValidUserId` (event-persist.ts:77) requires `[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}`, i.e. uppercase Crockford base32. The loader produces ids that would fail that check.

Decision (user): tolerate the inconsistent casing already in the log — do not normalise or rewrite history. Fix the source so new events stop introducing it.

- Keep the filename lowercased; stop treating it as the source of truth for the actor.
- Persist userId/userName in the event body, or carry a canonical id alongside the filename, so casing survives the round-trip.
- Must stay backward compatible with logs whose events have no in-body actor — those keep falling back to the filename.
- Check the same parse isn't relied on elsewhere (sync, merge, per-user log dedupe).
- TUI, GUI and MCP all read through this path, so the fix is shared.

Even when the underlying data is unchanged, latest is derived partly from Date.now() for the "all time" / offset-0 case, so the key can shift on a plain refresh and trigger a full ~760ms wave with no user action behind it.

Expected: the animation runs when the user changes something (scope, offset, board, series toggle) or on first mount — not as a side effect of background syncing.

Likely fix: stop keying the wrappers on a value that moves with wall-clock time. Either round/quantise the window key, or key on the user-controlled inputs (scope, offset, boardId, series) rather than on the derived window, or track "did the data actually change" and skip the remount when it didn't.

edit.description.md:
Found while verifying the picker (60025MM). Identity is correct — only the label disagrees.

`01KSAYRA4GHEKJP888WFBWBRDD` renders as:
- "test" in the contributor picker — `getBoardContributors` takes the most recent name from the event log.
- "jola" on the assignee chip — `getIssueAssignees` resolves the name from the contributor registry node.

Registry names are written once at create.contributor and never updated, so they go stale as soon as somebody changes their display name; the event log always carries the current one.

Touches GUI chips, MCP output and TUI rendering, so worth doing in one pass rather than per surface.

add.issue.comment.md:
Done at the API level. New `redact.contributor` event clears the display name and nothing else.

- Ordinary forward event: appended like any other, materialised by swapping the registry name for "removed contributor". No event is rewritten or removed, so the log stays append-only and every earlier event replays exactly as before.
- The id survives, so assignments keep resolving and nothing in history is orphaned — the issue stays assigned, to a nameless person.
- Refused for anyone who has authored events. Their name is written across every event they authored, so clearing the registry copy alone would leave the two sources disagreeing rather than removing anything. Only registry-only (external) contributors can be redacted.
- Exposed as MCP tool `epiq_contributor_redact`. `REDACTED_CONTRIBUTOR_NAME` is a shared constant so every surface shows the same placeholder.
- Adding the action to EVENT_ACTIONS made the compiler demand a materialize handler — the exhaustiveness check caught the omission before any test ran.

Verified on real data, including the part that matters: redacted gimli, then replayed the log from scratch. He comes back as "removed contributor", his original create.contributor event is *still in the log*, and exactly one redact event was appended (809 total). Redacting an author is refused.

Caveat worth stating plainly: this is redaction at projection, not erasure at rest. The name still sits inside the historical `create.contributor` payload in the log file — it stops being rendered anywhere, but it is not gone from disk. True erasure would mean rewriting history, which is exactly what this system must not do. If a hard-delete is ever required for a legal request, that is a different mechanism and a different conversation.

2 tests added. 316 pass. Typecheck + lint clean.

Not done: GUI and TUI affordances. Raised as its own ticket rather than folded in silently — redaction is a deliberate, rare action and deserves its own UI treatment.

edit.description.md:
Redaction exists at the API level (TBY4FEZ, MCP tool `epiq_contributor_redact`) but has no interface. Someone asked to have their name removed shouldn't require an MCP call.

- Offer it only where it applies: external contributors, since the API refuses anyone who has authored events.
- Needs a confirmation — it is irreversible in effect (the name is gone from every projection) even though the log is untouched.
- Show the "removed contributor" placeholder wherever assignees render, in both GUI chips and TUI views.
- Keep it out of the ordinary assign flow; this is an administrative action, not a way to tidy the list.

add.issue.comment.md:
Fixed by making the event log the source of truth for display names, with the registry as fallback.

A contributor node's name is written once at create.contributor and never updated, so it is a snapshot that goes stale the moment somebody changes their display name. The log always carries the current one — which is why the picker said "test" and the chip said "jola" for the same id.

- `getLatestNamesFromLog` builds an id -> latest-name map from state (no disk read), computed once per listing rather than per ticket.
- `getIssueAssignees` prefers that name, falling back to the registry.
- Same treatment in the TUI's AssigneeUI, which had the identical staleness.

The fallback direction matters for redaction: a redacted contributor has no events by definition (TBY4FEZ refuses authors), so the registry's "removed contributor" always wins and a redaction can never be undone by a stale log name.

Verified on real data: picker and chips both now read "test" across 10 assigned tickets, where the chip previously read "jola".
